C0.quote: the pairwise majority relation of this society is acyclic
C0.note: Borderline. The paper studies preference domains on which pairwise majority voting yields acyclic outcomes, i.e. properties of majority aggregation; coded ELIG on that basis.

C1.quote: suggest a new combinatorial interpretation of generalised Fishburn's domains
C1.note: Combinatorial and structural results on Condorcet domains: maximality, copiousness, single-peakedness on a circle. These could also be read as AX-type characterisations.

C2.1.value: preferences ... represented by linear orders; domain of linear orders
C2.1.quote: have preferences over those alternatives represented by linear orders

C2.2.quote: By L(A) we will denote all linear orders on the set

C2.3.quote: all voters of a certain society are known to have preferences
C2.3.note: Voters' preferences are the held attitude.

C2.4.quote: the pairwise majority relation of this society is acyclic
C2.4.note: The majority relation is computed directly from preferences, with no statement about submission or reporting.

C4.1.note: No utility-type notions are used for voters.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: The individual freedom remark appears only in the introduction.

VOT.note: Voters appear only as holders of preferences that define domains; no voter action is modelled.

claims.quote: allows a society to always have transitive collective decisions
provide voters with as much individual freedom as possible

C9.2.note: For transitive collective decisions to follow from acyclicity of the majority relation over preferences, voters must submit their preferences sincerely; this is not stated.
